races.title: State Senate, District 10
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Linda R. Price
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Senate District 10 in 2026. Small business owner and educator. Began her career with the Department of Defense, worked in human resources and organizational development, and founded a consulting firm. Has been an adjunct professor at Bay Area colleges for 30+ years. Ran for a school board seat in 2022 and lost.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists endorsements from the Republican Party of California and Reform California, along with several voter-guide recommendations.
In her own Ballotpedia survey she says the American Independent Party, Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association and California Cities for Local Control have endorsed her (self-reported).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Linda Price was born or raised, or the year she moved to California. We found no record of elected office, no bills, no documented actions on the platform topics, and no statements on data centers, property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. Her campaign site speaks generally of streamlining responsible development and expanding housing, but gives no specifics. We found no news coverage or documented controversies about her.

local.label: Roots 55: Her 2022 Ballotpedia survey says she has been part of the Fremont Union High School District community since 1970, and she earned an associate degree at Foothill-De Anza Community College in 1974; her birthplace and upbringing are not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Small business owner who founded an organizational consulting firm serving high-tech and other industries. Earlier worked in human resources and organizational development, and began her career with the Department of Defense. Adjunct professor at seven Bay Area colleges for 30+ years. Has held no elected office; lost a 2022 school board race.
qual.why: Business ownership and management experience puts her in the middle range. She has no legislative service and no policy or budget career, and the record shows no elected office.
qual.label: Business ownership and management experience puts her in the middle range. She has no legislative service and no policy or budget career, and the record shows no elected office.

back-police-order.evidence: Says she supports strong partnerships between law enforcement and communities, holding criminals accountable, and making sure first responders have the resources they need.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)

cands.name: Scott Sakakihara
cands.bio: Union City councilmember since 2022 and former vice mayor. Harvard-trained attorney and U.S. Navy Reserve intelligence officer. Former Union City planning commissioner, with earlier White House and congressional internships. Won the State Senate District 10 race in November 2026.

endorsements.text: Self-reported in his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey: Alameda County Firefighters (IAFF Local 55), Building and Construction Trades Council of Alameda County, Teamsters Joint Council 7, California AAPI Legislative Caucus, State Senator Jesse Arreguín, and former Congressman Mike Honda.

cands.gaps: We found no stated position or record from him on data centers, property taxes on homes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, guns, or school vouchers and charters. We could not find any of his Union City Council votes, so what he did in office is known only from his own campaign descriptions. His specific employer and role in the private sector are not confirmed by a primary source. The campaign's Issues page was cut off, so some of its text could not be read.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says he was born and raised in Union City, and his campaign site says he grew up there and attended local public schools, including Pioneer Elementary.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Union City councilmember since 2022 and former vice mayor, after serving on the Union City Planning Commission. Harvard Law graduate (2008) and Navy Reserve intelligence officer. His campaign says he spent nearly a decade as chief of staff of a tech company's finance department, managing a $1.8 billion budget. He has not served in a state legislature.
qual.why: Local elected office, a law degree and budget-management experience put him in the middle-to-upper part of the middle band. He has no prior legislative service or chamber leadership, and the budget role comes from his campaign's own account.
qual.label: Local elected office, a law degree and budget-management experience put him in the middle-to-upper part of the middle band. He has no prior legislative service or chamber leadership, and the budget role comes from his campaign's own account.

back-police-order.evidence: Says that on the City Council he helped hire more police officers and community service workers, protected public safety funding, and helped increase police staffing by 30%, alongside community-oriented policing.

workers-first.evidence: Says he has opposed Trump's ICE raids, fought locally for funding for immigrant communities, and will defend immigrants in the State Senate.

pro-life.evidence: Says he will stand up for women in need of reproductive healthcare and defend reproductive freedom in the State Senate.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says he helped streamline regulations to make it easier to build multi-family and affordable homes, and supports building more infill housing near transit.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 4 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised

roots.summary: Wikipedia says he was born and raised in Union City, and his campaign site says he grew up there and attended local public schools, including Pioneer Elementary.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Campaign site says he helped streamline regulations to make it easier to build multi-family and affordable homes. In his Ballotpedia survey he names more affordable and market-rate housing and infill housing near transit as priorities.
